clue.text: Generous loan requested by Antony for Noddy's friend?

definitions.meaning: Mark Antony's speech in Julius Caesar opens 'lend me your ears', so a generous loan of them would be large lugs
in Enid Blyton's children's books the toy Noddy's best friend is a bearded brownie with large ears

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader wonders what Antony borrowed and what it has to do with a children's character.
explanation.walkthrough: Noddy is a much-loved British children's book character by Enid Blyton; his companion's name is the answer, and the Shakespeare line supplies the other reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of Noddy's gnome-like companion in the Blyton stories is exactly this pair of words.

clue.text: Forlorn French leader in Basque cap

indicators.note: in means the leading letter sits inside the cap

parts.note: a beret is the flat cap associated with the Basques

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of French

explanation.surface: A downcast French chief wears a beret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' picks F from French; 'in' puts it inside BERET.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means deprived and desolate, so forlorn.

clue.text: Girl from Conwy's last seen in the valleys

indicators.note: seen in places the letter inside the valleys

parts.note: glens are valleys

indicators.note: last means the final letter of Conwy

explanation.surface: A girl from the Welsh town of Conwy was last spotted in the valleys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' picks Y from Conwy; 'seen in' puts it inside GLENS. Conwy is a town in Wales, where the name is common.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenys is a Welsh girl's name.

clue.text: Santa in big buggy not letting anyone get cross?

indicators.note: buggy, as faulty software is buggy, says the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Father Christmas in a large pram refuses to let anyone become angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' shuffles SANTA IN BIG. 'Cross' is the X on a ballot paper, not anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone declining to vote puts no X on the ballot paper, so no cross is made.

clue.text: Family member in charge of sound

parts.note: a son is a family member

explanation.surface: A relative is responsible for the audio.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic is the adjective relating to sound.

clue.text: Belt for cunning planner when king is deposed

indicators.note: a deposed king is removed from his throne, so the letter for king is taken out of the planner's name

parts.note: Baldrick is the servant in the TV comedy Blackadder, forever announcing he has a cunning plan
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A belt is named after a scheming character once the monarch has been overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackadder is a British TV comedy; its dogsbody Baldrick's catchphrase is 'I have a cunning plan'. Dropping K leaves the sword belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt worn over one shoulder to carry a sword or bugle.

clue.text: Squash and spread fruitcake

parts.note: butter is a spread
fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, a nut

explanation.surface: A cook mashes a cake and spreads it.
explanation.definitionFit: Butternut is a variety of squash with pale orange flesh.

clue.text: John's given time to produce ill-gotten gains

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a loo

explanation.surface: A man named John is allowed time to come up with stolen money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name, but it is slang for the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is stolen goods or money obtained dishonestly.

clue.text: Again be seen to harvest fruit

parts.note: to reap is to harvest
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is seen once more gathering fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to come into view once more.

clue.text: Chop a pine and leave quickly

parts.note: to chop is to cut
to pine is to long for

explanation.surface: A lumberjack fells a pine tree and hurries away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like a tree, but it is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut along is an informal way of saying to go away quickly.

clue.text: Rook takes heart from others — because these birds won't fly

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here the middle two of the six in others

parts.note: as can mean because, as in 'as it was late'

explanation.surface: A rook steals courage from other birds, which explains why they stay grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart from' takes the middle HE of OTHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheas are large South American birds that cannot fly, like ostriches and emus.

clue.text: Wait to toss fan out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, telling us the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to throw their admirer out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles TO TOSS FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation asks someone to pause before acting, which is what the command wait does.

clue.text: Bird, insect, mammal? One that sings

parts.note: a fly is an insect
a cat is a mammal
Cher is a famous American singer

explanation.surface: A list of creatures ends with a question about which of them is a songster.
explanation.definitionFit: Flycatchers are small perching songbirds that catch insects in flight.

clue.text: Motor manufacturer held back by unfavourable position

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A car maker finds itself hampered by a poor market position.
explanation.walkthrough: The run LEPO spans 'unfavourable position'; 'held back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opel is a German car maker, a well-known motor manufacturer.

clue.text: Hopeless admirer of female found a spouse

indicators.note: hopeless means in a hopeless mess, so the letters of admirer are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lovelorn suitor of a woman discovers she has a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopeless' looks like it describes the admirer's chances but signals the shuffle of ADMIRER; the lovelorn picture hides the plain sense of having been wed.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry someone off is to find them a husband or wife.

clue.text: Occasionally win after turning on fish?

indicators.note: after places the word for win at the end, behind the other pieces
turning means the little word on is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Wanda is the fish of the film A Fish Called Wanda
to gain is to win

explanation.surface: An angler wonders whether success comes only after switching on the fish finder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses ON and 'after' puts the word for win at the end. Wanda is the fish from the film A Fish Called Wanda, the crossword's favourite fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from time to time, so it is a synonym for occasionally.

clue.text: I see a worm turn — it's so boring!

indicators.note: turn means the letters change round into a new order

explanation.surface: Watching a worm wriggle is so dull it prompts a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' shuffles I SEE A WORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearisome means tiresome and tedious, a synonym of boring.

clue.text: Damned ringleader framed by one on trial

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded, so the leader letter goes inside

parts.note: the accused is the person on trial
the leading letter of ring is R

explanation.surface: A gang's ringleader is set up by someone facing charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' is the first letter of ring; 'framed by' puts it inside ACCUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means under a curse, so damned.

clue.text: Way to play in musical rejected by Roman statesman

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the musical's name is read backwards

parts.note: Cats is the Lloyd Webber musical
Cato was a Roman statesman

explanation.surface: A Roman politician turns down a role in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses CATS to STAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a musical direction to play notes short and detached.

clue.text: Shrub in bed with a single flower

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
one means single
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a bush in a bed alongside one bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is a common garden shrub with small leaves and red berries.

clue.text: Mike's novel? "Love in a Cold Climate", one's found

definitions.text: in a Cold Climate", one's found

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A man called Mike is reading the Nancy Mitford novel Love in a Cold Climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' shuffles MIKES into ESKIM. Love in a Cold Climate is a Nancy Mitford novel, but here 'Love' gives O and the rest defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit peoples (the dated term being this word) live in Arctic regions, a cold climate.

clue.text: Movement uniting female soldier with second-in-command

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
GI is an American soldier
read as the second letter in command, which is O

explanation.surface: A woman soldier is joined with the deputy leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-in-command' means the second letter of 'command', not a deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a slow movement of a symphony or other musical work.

clue.text: A French officer is remarkable north of the border

parts.note: un is French for a
CO stands for commanding officer

explanation.surface: A French officer is described as extraordinary in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means in Scotland, i.e. Scots usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, unco means strange or extraordinary, so remarkable in Scottish speech.

clue.text: Upset with shaven head?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., having one's tresses (hair) taken away

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy after having all their hair shaved off.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means upset, anxious or in pain, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Figure worshipped by child upset me

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: A child's idol makes an adult cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or figure revered as a sacred emblem.

clue.text: Doing nothing — taking some unpaid leave

indicators.note: taking some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A worker is idle while on unpaid time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means inactive, not working or doing anything.

clue.text: Bear with short pole catches the eye

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: south is one of the Earth's poles

explanation.surface: A bear holding a stubby pole draws attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the H from SOUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand out is to be conspicuous, so it catches the eye.

clue.text: Due opinion?

definitions.meaning: due means still to be paid
split as O plus pinion, and a pinion is a bird's wing, giving O plus wing

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a view is what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits 'opinion' into O and PINION; pinion means wing, so O + WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing describes a debt that remains unpaid, which is what due means.

clue.text: See seed knocked out — sports officials intervene

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so the officials go inside the rearranged seed
knocked out suggests something battered out of shape, so the letters of seed are rearranged

parts.note: IOC is the International Olympic Committee

explanation.surface: A seeded player is knocked out of a tournament and the sporting authorities step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' rearranges SEED into DESE and 'intervene' slips the officials inside. 'See' is not about looking: a bishop's see is his diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the area under a bishop's authority, which is a diocese.

clue.text: Old Communist leader accepts fair odds — like this gangster

indicators.note: accepts means the leader takes the odd letters inside him

parts.note: Mao Zedong led Communist China

indicators.note: odds picks the odd letters, first and third, of fair

parts.note: so means in this way

explanation.surface: An old Communist ruler accepts fair odds, as a gangster might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' takes the odd letters of 'fair' and 'accepts' sets them inside the leader's name; 'fair odds' reads like betting talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A mafioso is a member of the Mafia, the Sicilian-American crime organisation.
